vāyuryamo'gnirvaruṇaḥ śaśāṅkaḥ |
prajāpatistvaṃ prapitāmahaśca |
namo namaste'stu sahasrakṛtvaḥ |
punaśca bhūyo'pi namo namaste ||
english: You are Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna and the moon; you are Prajapati, and the great-grandfather of all. Salutations to you a thousand times, and again and again, salutations!

school_notes.note: You are the father even of Brahmā, and so the great-grandfather of all.
Hiraṇyagarbha is the grandfather of creatures; as his father, you are their great-grandfather.

speaker: Arjuna
context: Arjuna offers salutations in every direction to Krishna, who pervades all.

नमः पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्ते ।
नमोऽस्तु ते सर्वत एव सर्व ।
अनन्तवीर्यामितविक्रमस्त्वं ।
सर्वं समाप्नोषि ततोऽसि सर्वः ॥
iast:
namaḥ purastādatha pṛṣṭhataste |
namo'stu te sarvata eva sarva |
anantavīryāmitavikramastvaṃ |
sarvaṃ samāpnoṣi tato'si sarvaḥ ||
english: Salutations to you in front and behind; salutations to you on every side, you who are all. Your power is infinite and your might immeasurable; you pervade everything, and so you are everything.

school_notes.note: Salutations in the east and behind you, and on every side, to you who are everywhere.
You pervade all things as their self, so all things are modes of you, and you are 'all'.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Arjuna
context: Arjuna asks forgiveness for having treated Krishna too casually as a friend (11.41-11.44).
devanagari:
सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तं ।
हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति ।
अजानता महिमानं तवेदं ।
मया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि ॥

sakheti matvā prasabhaṃ yaduktaṃ |

ajānatā mahimānaṃ tavedaṃ |
mayā pramādātpraṇayena vāpi ||
english: Whatever I said rashly, thinking of you as a friend, "Hey Krishna! Hey Yadava! Hey friend!", not knowing this greatness of yours, out of carelessness or out of affection,

school_notes.note: Thinking of you as a friend my own age, I spoke rashly, not knowing your greatness as the Lord with the universal form.
Not knowing your infinite power and your being the self and creator of all, out of confusion or long familiarity I treated you as 'my companion'.

speaker: Arjuna
context: Arjuna continues asking forgiveness for past disrespect.
devanagari:
यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसि ।
विहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु ।
एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षं ।
तत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् ॥
iast:
yaccāvahāsārthamasatkṛto'si |
vihāraśayyāsanabhojaneṣu |
eko'thavāpyacyuta tatsamakṣaṃ |
tatkṣāmaye tvāmahamaprameyam ||
english: and whatever disrespect I showed you in jest, while playing, resting, sitting or eating, alone or in front of others, Krishna, for all that I ask your forgiveness, immeasurable one.

school_notes.note: Whatever disrespect I showed you in jest, during play, rest, sitting or meals, in private or in company, I beg your forgiveness.

speaker: Arjuna
context: Arjuna praises Krishna as the father and teacher of the world, without equal.

पितासि लोकस्य चराचरस्य ।
त्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान् ।
न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कुतोऽन्यो ।
लोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभाव ॥
iast:
pitāsi lokasya carācarasya |
tvamasya pūjyaśca gururgarīyān |
na tvatsamo'styabhyadhikaḥ kuto'nyo |
lokatraye'pyapratimaprabhāva ||
english: You are the father of the world, of all that moves and does not move; you are its object of worship and its greatest teacher. No one in the three worlds equals you; how could anyone surpass you, whose power has no equal?

school_notes.note: You are not only the father of the world but worthy of worship, being the greatest teacher; no one equals you.
No one in the three worlds equals you, let alone surpasses you, in compassion or in anything else.

speaker: Arjuna
context: Arjuna asks Krishna to forgive him as a father, friend or lover forgives.
devanagari:
तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायं ।
प्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम् ।
पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युः ।
प्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम् ॥
iast:
tasmātpraṇamya praṇidhāya kāyaṃ |
prasādaye tvāmahamīśamīḍyam |
piteva putrasya sakheva sakhyuḥ |
priyaḥ priyāyārhasi deva soḍhum ||
english: So, bowing down and prostrating my body, I ask your grace, Lord who is to be praised. As a father bears with a son, a friend with a friend, a lover with the beloved, so please bear with me, O God.

school_notes.note: As a father forgives his son's faults, a friend a friend's, and a lover the beloved's, so bear with me.
As a father or friend is won over by someone who bows and asks forgiveness, even after doing wrong, so you, supremely compassionate, should bear with everything I have done.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Arjuna
context: Arjuna, both thrilled and frightened, asks to see Krishna's familiar form again (11.45-11.46).
devanagari:
अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वा ।
भयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे ।
तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपं ।
प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥
iast:
adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ hṛṣito'smi dṛṣṭvā |
bhayena ca pravyathitaṃ mano me |
tadeva me darśaya deva rūpaṃ |
prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa ||
english: I am thrilled to have seen what was never seen before, yet my mind is shaken with fear. Show me that other form of yours, O God; be gracious, lord of gods, refuge of the world.

school_notes.note: Show me the form that is my friend.
I rejoice at seeing your form, never seen before, but my mind is shaken with fear; show me again your gentle, gracious form.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Arjuna
context: Arjuna asks Krishna to return to his four-armed form.
devanagari:
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रहस्त- ।
मिच्छामि त्वां द्रष्टुमहं तथैव ।
तेनैव रूपेण चतुर्भुजेन ।
सहस्रबाहो भव विश्वमूर्ते ॥
iast:
kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakrahasta- |
micchāmi tvāṃ draṣṭumahaṃ tathaiva |
tenaiva rūpeṇa caturbhujena |
sahasrabāho bhava viśvamūrte ||
english: I wish to see you as before, wearing a crown, holding a mace, discus in hand. Take on that four-armed form, thousand-armed one, whose body is the universe.

school_notes.note: Become again that four-armed form, the son of Vasudeva.
Take again your earlier four-armed form, you who now appear thousand-armed, with the universe as your body.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna tells Arjuna the vision was a gift of grace, granted to no one before (11.47-11.48).
devanagari:
मया प्रसन्नेन तवार्जुनेदं ।
रूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात् ।
तेजोमयं विश्वमनन्तमाद्यं ।
यन्मे त्वदन्येन न दृष्टपूर्वम् ॥
iast:
mayā prasannena tavārjunedaṃ |
rūpaṃ paraṃ darśitamātmayogāt |
tejomayaṃ viśvamanantamādyaṃ |
yanme tvadanyena na dṛṣṭapūrvam ||
english: Out of grace, Arjuna, through my own power, I have shown you this supreme form, made of light, universal, infinite and first of all, which no one but you has ever seen.

school_notes.note: Grace here means my wish to favour you; with it I showed you this form by the power of my own lordship.
This form, full of radiance, the self of all, without beginning, middle or end, the source of everything, has been seen by no one else.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says no ritual, study or austerity can win this vision on its own.
devanagari:
न वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैर्न दानै- ।
र्न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रैः ।
एवंरूपः शक्य अहं नृलोके ।
द्रष्टुं त्वदन्येन कुरुप्रवीर ॥
iast:
na vedayajñādhyayanairna dānai- |
rna ca kriyābhirna tapobhirugraiḥ |
evaṃrūpaḥ śakya ahaṃ nṛloke |
draṣṭuṃ tvadanyena kurupravīra ||
english: Not through the Vedas, sacrifice or study, not through gifts, rituals or severe austerities can I be seen in this form in the human world by anyone but you, hero of the Kurus.

school_notes.note: Not by studying the four Vedas, by great gifts, by rites or by harsh austerities can I be seen in this form.
No one without wholehearted devotion to me can see me as I am through the Vedas, sacrifices and the like alone.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna reassures the frightened Arjuna and returns to his familiar form.
devanagari:
मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो ।
दृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम् ।
व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वं ।
तदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य ॥
iast:
mā te vyathā mā ca vimūḍhabhāvo |
dṛṣṭvā rūpaṃ ghoramīdṛṅmamedam |
vyapetabhīḥ prītamanāḥ punastvaṃ |
tadeva me rūpamidaṃ prapaśya ||
english: Do not be afraid or bewildered at seeing this terrible form of mine. Free of fear and glad at heart, see again this form of mine.

school_notes.note: Let there be no fear or bewilderment; free of fear and glad of mind, see again my four-armed form with conch, discus and mace.
Let the distress and bewilderment caused by this terrible form be gone; I will show you the gentle form you already know.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sanjaya
context: Sanjaya reports that Krishna resumed his gentle form and comforted Arjuna.
devanagari:
इत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वा ।
स्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः ।
आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनं ।
भूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा ॥
iast:
ityarjunaṃ vāsudevastathoktvā |
svakaṃ rūpaṃ darśayāmāsa bhūyaḥ |
āśvāsayāmāsa ca bhītamenaṃ |
bhūtvā punaḥ saumyavapurmahātmā ||
english: Having spoken to Arjuna in this way, Krishna showed his own form again; and the great one, taking on his gentle form once more, comforted the frightened Arjuna.

school_notes.note: He showed again his form born in Vasudeva's house and, becoming gentle in body, comforted the frightened Arjuna.
Vasudeva's son showed his own four-armed form again and, taking his familiar gentle shape, comforted Arjuna, who had been frightened by the unfamiliar form.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Arjuna
context: Arjuna, calmed by the sight of Krishna's gentle form, regains his composure.
devanagari:
दृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तव सौम्यं जनार्दन ।
इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः ॥
iast:
dṛṣṭvedaṃ mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ tava saumyaṃ janārdana |
idānīmasmi saṃvṛttaḥ sacetāḥ prakṛtiṃ gataḥ ||
english: Seeing this gentle human form of yours, Krishna, I am now myself again; my mind is calm and I have returned to my normal state.

school_notes.note: Seeing your gentle human form, my friend's form, I am composed and myself again.
Seeing your gentle human form, unmatched in beauty and grace, I have come to my senses and returned to my natural state.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna tells Arjuna how rare the vision he received is (11.52-11.54).

सुदुर्दर्शमिदं रूपं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम ।
देवा अप्यस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः ॥
iast:
sudurdarśamidaṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭavānasi yanmama |
devā apyasya rūpasya nityaṃ darśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ ||
english: This form of mine that you have seen is very hard to see; even the gods long always to see it.

school_notes.note: Even the gods, who always long to see this form, have not seen it as you have, nor will they.
This form, which rules, supports and causes everything, can be seen by no one; even the gods long for it but have not seen it.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna repeats that no outward practice alone can bring this vision.
devanagari:
नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया ।
शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा ॥

nāhaṃ vedairna tapasā na dānena na cejyayā |
śakya evaṃvidho draṣṭuṃ dṛṣṭavānasi māṃ yathā ||
english: Not through the Vedas, nor austerity, nor gifts, nor sacrifice can I be seen as you have seen me.

school_notes.note: Not by the four Vedas, by austerities such as the lunar fast, by gifts of cows, land and gold, or by sacrifice or worship.
Vedic study, sacrifice, gifts and austerities without devotion to me cannot bring the sight of me as I truly am.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna names the one way to know, see and enter him: undivided devotion.
devanagari:
भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्य अहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन ।
ज्ञातुं द्रष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप ॥

bhaktyā tvananyayā śakya ahamevaṃvidho'rjuna |
jñātuṃ draṣṭuṃ ca tattvena praveṣṭuṃ ca paraṃtapa ||
english: But by undivided devotion, Arjuna, I can be known in this form, truly seen, and entered into, scorcher of enemies.

school_notes.note: Undivided devotion is devotion never apart from the Lord, through which nothing but Vāsudeva is perceived by any of the senses.
By undivided devotion alone I can be truly known through scripture, truly seen directly, and truly entered.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna closes chapter 11 with the devotee who reaches him: free of attachment and of ill will toward any being.
devanagari:
मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः ।
निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव ॥
iast:
matkarmakṛnmatparamo madbhaktaḥ saṅgavarjitaḥ |
nirvairaḥ sarvabhūteṣu yaḥ sa māmeti pāṇḍava ||
english: One who works for me, takes me as the highest goal, is devoted to me, is free of attachment and bears no ill will towards any being, comes to me, son of Pandu.

school_notes.note: Unlike a servant who works for a master but does not take him as the final goal, this person works for me and takes me as the highest goal; devoted, unattached and without enmity, they reach me.
One who does all actions, such as Vedic study, as worship of me, has me as the highest aim of every undertaking, and loves me intensely, reaches me.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Arjuna
context: Arjuna opens chapter 12, on devotion, asking which is better: worshipping Krishna in form or meditating on the formless Imperishable.
devanagari:
एवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते ।
ये चाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः ॥
iast:
evaṃ satatayuktā ye bhaktāstvāṃ paryupāsate |
ye cāpyakṣaramavyaktaṃ teṣāṃ ke yogavittamāḥ ||

school_notes.note: 'In this way' points back to 11.55: those wholly devoted to the Lord meditate on the universal form; others, having renounced all desires, meditate on the imperishable Brahman, free of all qualities.
Arjuna compares devotees who worship the Lord, full of every auspicious quality, as the highest goal, with those who meditate on the Imperishable, here the individual self in its own nature.
This chapter shows that worshipping the Lord is better than meditating on the unmanifest, and gives the means to it.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna answers that those who worship him with devoted, steady minds are the most disciplined.
devanagari:
मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते ।
श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः ॥
iast:
mayyāveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate |
śraddhayā parayopetāste me yuktatamā matāḥ ||
english: Those who fix their minds on me and worship me, always disciplined and endowed with supreme faith, I consider the most disciplined.

school_notes.note: Those who fix their minds on me, the universal form and lord of all masters of yoga, and worship me with supreme faith, spend their days and nights in me, so they are rightly called most disciplined.
Those who, out of intense love, fix their minds on me with supreme faith are the most disciplined: they reach me easily and soon.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna turns to those who meditate on the formless Imperishable (12.3-12.5).
devanagari:
ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते ।
सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यं च कूटस्थमचलं ध्रुवम् ॥
iast:
ye tvakṣaramanirdeśyamavyaktaṃ paryupāsate |
sarvatragamacintyaṃ ca kūṭasthamacalaṃ dhruvam ||
english: But those who worship the Imperishable, which cannot be defined, the unmanifest, all-pervading, beyond thought, unchanging, unmoving and constant,

school_notes.note: The Imperishable cannot be described because it is unmanifest, revealed by no means of knowledge; worship means approaching it as scripture teaches and dwelling on it in an unbroken stream, like flowing oil.
The Imperishable here is the individual self: indefinable by words like 'god' or 'human' because it is other than the body, present in every body yet unlike them, and the same in all.
Answers what fruit others gain; citing the Bhāgavata, it is māyā (prakṛti) that is called indefinable.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says those who meditate on the formless also reach him, through self-control and care for all beings.
devanagari:
संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः ।
ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥
iast:
saṃniyamyendriyagrāmaṃ sarvatra samabuddhayaḥ |
te prāpnuvanti māmeva sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ ||
english: restraining all the senses, even-minded everywhere, delighting in the welfare of all beings, they too reach me.

school_notes.note: Withdrawing the senses, even-minded at gain and loss, devoted to the good of all, they reach me; there is nothing more to say about them, since the wise are my very self (7.18).

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna explains why the path of the formless is harder for embodied beings.
devanagari:
क्लेशोऽधिकतरस्तेषामव्यक्तासक्तचेतसाम् ।
अव्यक्ता हि गतिर्दुःखं देहवद्भिरवाप्यते ॥
iast:
kleśo'dhikatarasteṣāmavyaktāsaktacetasām |
avyaktā hi gatirduḥkhaṃ dehavadbhiravāpyate ||
english: The difficulty is greater for those whose minds are set on the unmanifest, for the unmanifest goal is hard for embodied beings to reach.

school_notes.note: The difficulty is greater for them because they must give up identifying with the body; the goal of the unmanifest is hard for the embodied.
Those who identify with the body find it hard to turn the mind to the unmanifest self, since they take the body to be the self.
The path to him through meditation on the unmanifest is hard, needing intense practice, mastery of all the senses, equal vision and devotion to Viṣṇu.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes those who offer all actions to him and meditate on him with single-minded devotion (12.6-12.7).
devanagari:

अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते ॥

ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparāḥ |
ananyenaiva yogena māṃ dhyāyanta upāsate ||
english: But those who surrender all actions to me, take me as the highest, and worship me, meditating on me with undivided yoga,

school_notes.note: Those who give up all actions to me and meditate on me with yoga that rests on nothing else but the universal form.
Those who offer to me all ordinary actions for sustaining the body, and all Vedic rites, and meditate on me with yoga that has no other goal.

context: Krishna continues: knowledge includes steady devotion and a liking for solitude.

school_notes.note: Unwavering devotion grounded in the settled conviction that there is nothing higher than Vāsudeva; resorting to places pure by nature or made pure.
Steady devotion to me, the Lord of all, through single-minded yoga; living in places free of people, and finding no pleasure in crowds.

context: Krishna concludes the list: these qualities are what true knowledge means.

एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतोऽन्यथा ॥

english: constancy in knowledge of the self, and insight into the purpose of true knowledge: this is called knowledge, and whatever is contrary to it is ignorance.

These qualities, from humility on, are called 'knowledge' because they are the means by which the self is known.
'Insight into the purpose of true knowledge' means studying scripture in order to gain direct knowledge.

context: Krishna turns to what is to be known: the beginningless Brahman (13.12-13.17).

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes what is to be known as present everywhere, with every faculty in every place.

The pure self can do the work of hands and feet everywhere, as the Upanishad says of Brahman: 'without hands or feet it moves and grasps'.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes the paradoxes of what is to be known: sense-like yet without senses, beyond the gunas yet experiencing them.

sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitam |

english: It seems to have the qualities of all the senses, yet is free of all the senses; unattached, yet sustaining all; free of the gunas, yet experiencing the gunas.

school_notes.note: It appears through the senses and the mind, which are its adjuncts, yet in itself it has no senses.
It can know objects through the activity of the senses, yet by its own nature knows everything without any senses.
It is the one that illumines all the senses and the gunas.

context: Krishna continues: what is to be known is both within and beyond all things, near and far.

bahirantaśca bhūtānāmacaraṃ carameva ca |

english: It is outside and inside beings, unmoving and moving; it is too subtle to be known; it is far away, and also near.

school_notes.note: 'Outside' and 'inside' are spoken relative to the body wrongly taken as the self; being subtle, like space, it is not known by the unwise.
It is outside the elements, being without a body, and also inside them; unmoving by nature, yet moving when embodied; and unknowable because of its subtlety.

bhūtabhartṛ ca tajjñeyaṃ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca ||
english: Undivided, it seems divided among beings; it is to be known as the sustainer of beings, the one who devours them and the one who brings them forth.

school_notes.note: Like space, it is one in all bodies though it appears divided; it sustains beings, devours them at dissolution, and brings them forth at creation.
The self is undivided in its nature as knower, though those who do not understand see it as divided into god, human and so on.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes what is to be known as the light of all lights, dwelling in every heart.

jyotiṣāmapi tajjyotistamasaḥ paramucyate |
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam ||
english: It is the light of all lights, said to be beyond darkness; it is knowledge, what is to be known, and the goal of knowledge, dwelling in the heart of all.

school_notes.note: It is by the light of the self's consciousness that the sun and other lights shine, as the Upanishad says.
The self's own light of knowledge illumines even lamps and the sun, which only dispel the darkness between the senses and their objects.

iti kṣetraṃ tathā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ coktaṃ samāsataḥ |
madbhakta etadvijñāya madbhāvāyopapadyate ||
english: So the field, knowledge and what is to be known have been described in brief. My devotee who understands this comes to my state of being.

school_notes.note: This, in brief, is the whole meaning of the Veda and of the Gita.
Sums up: the field (13.5-13.6), the means to knowledge (13.7-13.11), and what is to be known (13.12-13.17).
The means to knowledge were given first because they are so many and so useful, and because they include the changes.

context: Krishna introduces nature and the person, both without beginning (13.19-13.23).

english: Know that both nature and the person are without beginning; and know that the changes and the gunas arise from nature.

Prakṛti and the person are both beginningless and joined to each other; the desire and aversion that bind, and the humility and other qualities that free, both arise from prakṛti.
The gunas are sattva and the rest; the 'changes' are named separately as their slightly developed forms.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna explains the division of roles: nature acts, while the person experiences.

english: Nature is said to be the cause of the body, the senses and agency; the person is said to be the cause of experiencing pleasure and pain.

Prakṛti, governed by the person, is the cause of the body and senses acting; the person's part is only to govern it.
The person experiences because it is conscious; prakṛti, being inert, is what changes.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says attachment to nature's qualities is what drives rebirth.

kāraṇaṃ guṇasaṅgo'sya sadasadyonijanmasu ||
english: The person, abiding in nature, experiences the gunas born of nature; attachment to the gunas is the cause of its births in good and bad wombs.

school_notes.note: 'Abiding in nature' means identifying with prakṛti; attachment to its gunas causes birth in higher and lower bodies.
The person, whose own nature is the joy of experiencing itself, when joined with prakṛti experiences the pleasure and pain born of the gunas; attachment to them causes rebirth.

upadraṣṭānumantā ca bhartā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ |

context: Krishna says knowing nature and the person truly frees one from rebirth.

english: One who knows the person and nature, together with the gunas, in this way, is not born again, however they may live.

One who rightly discerns the person and prakṛti is not again bound to prakṛti, even if living in great hardship in any kind of body.

english: Some see the self in the self by the self through meditation; others through the yoga of knowledge; and others through the yoga of action.

Those whose yoga is complete see the self through devotional meditation; others make the mind ready through the yoga of knowledge; others through the yoga of action.
'Sankhya' here means knowledge of the Lord's nature as the Veda teaches it.

english: Still others, not knowing this, worship after hearing it from others; they too, devoted to what they have heard, cross beyond death.

english: Whatever is born, moving or unmoving, know that it arises from the union of the field and its knower, best of the Bharatas.

english: One who sees the supreme Lord abiding equally in all beings, not perishing when they perish, truly sees.

Seeing the Lord, the self, as the same in all, one does not harm oneself but protects oneself and is freed from worldly existence.

context: Krishna says true seeing recognises that nature acts while the self is not the doer.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna compares the knower of the field to the sun lighting up the world.

english: As the one sun lights up this whole world, so the owner of the field lights up the whole field, Arjuna.

school_notes.note: The owner of the field is the Supreme Self: one in all fields, like the sun, and untouched by them.

Those who know the difference between field and knower, and the means to freedom from prakṛti (humility and the rest), reach the self, freed of bondage.
Sums up the chapter: field and knower differ as inert and conscious, doer and non-doer, changing and unchanging.

context: Krishna opens chapter 14, on the three qualities of nature (gunas), promising the highest knowledge.

यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः ॥

A further teaching, still within the subject of nature and the person: the knowledge of the gunas, sattva and the rest, which is the best of all knowledge about prakṛti and the person.
The remaining chapters mainly teach the means.

context: Krishna says those who take refuge in this knowledge share his nature and are free of birth and dissolution.

context: Krishna describes great nature as the womb into which he places the seed of all beings (14.3-14.4).

'Great Brahman' is prakṛti, which takes the forms of Śrī, Bhū and Durgā; goddesses such as Umā and Sarasvatī are other beings who share a portion of it.

context: Krishna calls nature the mother and himself the seed-giving father of every living form.

Of the forms born among gods, humans, animals and plants, prakṛti joined by me with the conscious beings is the cause, and I am the father who sows the seed.

context: Krishna names the three gunas and says they bind the self to the body (14.5-14.9).

iast:
sattvaṃ rajastama iti guṇāḥ prakṛtisaṃbhavāḥ |
nibadhnanti mahābāho dehe dehinamavyayam ||
english: Sattva, rajas and tamas, the gunas born of nature, bind the imperishable embodied one to the body, mighty-armed one.

Shows how bondage works, so that one can take up the means to freedom.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes sattva: pure and illuminating, yet still binding through attachment to happiness and knowledge.
devanagari:

सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ ॥
iast:
tatra sattvaṃ nirmalatvātprakāśakamanāmayam |
sukhasaṅgena badhnāti jñānasaṅgena cānagha ||
english: Of these, sattva, being pure, is illuminating and free of affliction; it binds, sinless one, through attachment to happiness and attachment to knowledge.

school_notes.note: Clear like crystal, sattva illumines; it binds by making one cling to happiness, thinking 'I am happy', which falsely joins an object's quality to the self.
Sattva's purity is its freedom from anything that hides light and happiness; 'light' is knowing things as they are. It binds through attachment to that happiness and knowledge.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes rajas: passion born of craving, which binds through attachment to action.

iast:
rajo rāgātmakaṃ viddhi tṛṣṇāsaṅgasamudbhavam |
tannibadhnāti kaunteya karmasaṅgena dehinam ||
english: Know rajas to be passion, springing from craving and attachment; it binds the embodied one, son of Kunti, through attachment to action.

school_notes.note: Rajas colours the mind like red dye; craving is longing for what one lacks, attachment is the mind's clinging to what one has; rajas binds through attachment to action.
Rajas gives rise to desire between man and woman, to craving for all sense objects, and to clinging to sons, friends and relatives; it binds through attachment to action.
Rajas is the source of craving and attachment.

context: Krishna describes tamas: born of ignorance, deluding all, binding through carelessness, sloth and sleep.

tamastvajñānajaṃ viddhi mohanaṃ sarvadehinām |

english: But know tamas to be born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings; it binds, Arjuna, through carelessness, laziness and sleep.

school_notes.note: Tamas, born of ignorance, confuses all embodied beings and binds through carelessness, laziness and sleep.
'Ignorance' here is mistaken knowledge, the opposite of seeing things as they are; tamas produces it and binds through carelessness, laziness and sleep.
'Born of ignorance' means that ignorance is born of it, as 14.17 says.

context: Krishna sums up how each guna attaches a person: to happiness, to action, or to carelessness.

jñānamāvṛtya tu tamaḥ pramāde saṃjayatyuta ||
english: Sattva attaches one to happiness, rajas to action, Arjuna; but tamas, veiling knowledge, attaches one to carelessness.

Sattva mainly attaches to happiness, rajas to action, and tamas, hiding true knowledge, to acting against what should be done.

context: Krishna explains that the gunas compete, each rising by overpowering the other two.

english: Sattva rises by overpowering rajas and tamas, Arjuna; rajas, by overpowering sattva and tamas; and tamas likewise, by overpowering sattva and rajas.

school_notes.note: When sattva grows by overpowering the other two, it produces its own effects, knowledge and happiness; the same holds for rajas and tamas.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna gives the signs of each guna's dominance, starting with sattva (14.11-14.13).

english: When the light of knowledge shines through every gate of this body, then know that sattva is dominant.

school_notes.note: When the light of understanding arises through all the senses, the gates of perception, know by that sign that sattva has grown.
When knowledge revealing things as they are arises through the eyes and other gates, know that sattva has increased in this body.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna gives the signs of dominant rajas: greed, restlessness and craving.

रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥

Greed is reluctance to part with one's own wealth; activity is moving about with no purpose; restlessness is the senses never resting; longing is desire for objects.

english: Darkness, inertia, carelessness and delusion: these arise when tamas is dominant, joy of the Kurus.

school_notes.note: Lack of discernment, complete inactivity, carelessness and confusion are the signs that tamas has grown.

context: Krishna explains how the dominant guna at death shapes what follows (14.14-14.15).

Dying when sattva prevails, one is born among the pure, among those who truly know the self.

Dying in rajas, one is born in families who act for rewards; dying in tamas, one is born in deluded wombs such as dogs or pigs, unfit for any of life's goals.

context: Krishna describes the fruit of actions shaped by each guna.

'Pain' here means slight pleasure mixed with pain; he cites a text that from rajas comes some pleasure and some pain.

context: Krishna names what each guna produces: knowledge, greed, or carelessness and confusion.

context: Krishna says sattva leads upward, rajas keeps one in the middle, and tamas leads downward.

iast:

Going beyond sattva and the rest, and seeing the self as knowledge alone, one is freed from birth, death and old age and experiences the immortal self: this is 'my state'.

context: Krishna describes the one beyond the gunas, unmoved by their play (14.22-14.25).

english: One who does not resent light, activity or delusion when they arise, son of Pandu, nor long for them when they cease,

context: Krishna continues: such a person stays steady, like an onlooker, knowing it is only the gunas at work.

guṇā vartanta ityeva yo'vatiṣṭhati neṅgate ||

school_notes.note: Like a neutral onlooker who takes no side, the knower of the self is not shaken by the gunas, seeing them act upon one another.
Content in seeing the self as distinct from the gunas, such a person is indifferent elsewhere, and, reflecting that the gunas act in their own spheres, stays still.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna continues: the one beyond the gunas is the same in pain and pleasure, praise and blame.

तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः ॥

english: who is the same in pain and pleasure, rests in the self, regards a lump of earth, a stone and gold alike, is the same towards the pleasant and the unpleasant, steady, and the same in blame and praise,

school_notes.note: Pain and pleasure are the same to them; they rest serenely in their own self.
Loving the self above all, they are even-minded about the joys and sorrows of others such as children being born or dying, and so regard earth, stone and gold alike.

सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते ॥
iast:
mānāpamānayostulyastulyo mitrāripakṣayoḥ |
sarvārambhaparityāgī guṇātītaḥ sa ucyate ||
english: the same in honour and dishonour, the same towards friend and foe, having given up all self-centred undertakings: such a person is said to have gone beyond the gunas.

school_notes.note: The same towards friend and foe, even those who are neutral but seem so to others; having given up all undertakings aimed at seen or unseen rewards.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna gives the means of going beyond the gunas: unswerving devotion to him.

english: One who serves me with unswerving devotion goes beyond these gunas and becomes fit to become Brahman.

school_notes.note: Whoever, renunciant or person of action, serves me, Nārāyaṇa in the heart of all beings, with unfailing devotion, goes beyond the gunas and is fit to become Brahman.
Merely reflecting on the difference between prakṛti and the self will not overcome the gunas, since old contrary tendencies are strong; serving me with unswerving devotion does.
'Becoming Brahman' means becoming dear to the Lord as prakṛti is, though not to the same degree, citing the Padma Purāṇa.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna closes chapter 14: he is the ground of Brahman, of immortality, of eternal dharma and of perfect happiness.

english: For I am the foundation of Brahman, of the immortal and imperishable, of eternal dharma, and of absolute happiness.

school_notes.note: I, the inner self, am the foundation in which Brahman, the Supreme Self, rests: immortal, unchanging, eternal, and the absolute bliss.
Served with unswerving devotion, I am the ground of the immortal Brahman (the self), of eternal lordship, and of the absolute happiness of the wise.
'Brahman' here means māyā, prakṛti.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna opens chapter 15 with the image of worldly existence as an upside-down fig tree (15.1-15.4).

छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् ॥

ūrdhvamūlamadhaḥśākhamaśvatthaṃ prāhuravyayam |
chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni yastaṃ veda sa vedavit ||

school_notes.note: The tree of worldly existence has the unmanifest Brahman, endowed with the power of māyā, as its root 'above', being subtle, causal, eternal and great; he cites the Kaṭha Upaniṣad.
The tree is worldly existence, as the Kaṭha Upaniṣad describes; it is rooted above in four-faced Brahmā, who dwells beyond the seven worlds.
This chapter shows the nature of worldly existence and the means of going beyond it; 'above' is Viṣṇu, the highest, and 'aśvattha' means what does not stay the same even until tomorrow.

context: Krishna continues the image: the tree's branches are fed by the gunas, and its roots of action spread into the human world.

अधश्च मूलान्यनुसंततानि ।
कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके ॥

english: Its branches spread below and above, nourished by the gunas, with sense objects as their shoots; and below, its roots stretch out, binding to action in the human world.

The tree, rooted in Brahmā's world, ends in humans; its roots of karma spread into the human world, since actions done as humans lead to further births above and below.
The roots are the Lord's own forms; the Lord too gives fruit in keeping with karma.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says this tree's true form cannot be grasped, and it must be cut down with detachment (15.3-15.4).

अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूल- ।
मसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा ॥

na rūpamasyeha tathopalabhyate |

english: Its form is not perceived here as it really is: neither its end, nor its beginning, nor its foundation. Having cut down this firmly rooted fig tree with the strong axe of non-attachment,

school_notes.note: Its form is not found as described, since it is like a dream, a mirage or a city in the clouds, appearing and vanishing; so it has no end, beginning or middle that anyone can grasp.
People caught in worldly life do not perceive the tree this way; they know only 'I am a human, son of so-and-so'.
Its beginning and end is Viṣṇu; the axe is knowledge joined with non-attachment, and 'cutting' means discerning it.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna continues: after cutting the tree, one should seek the state of no return by taking refuge in the primal Person.

english: one should then seek that state from which those who reach it never return, thinking: "I take refuge in that primal Person from whom this ancient activity has flowed forth."

school_notes.note: Then seek that state of Viṣṇu from which none return, by taking refuge in the primal Person from whom the stream of worldly existence has flowed.
To cut the tree, take refuge in him alone; he cites a text that one who takes refuge in him neither grieves nor rejoices, is neither born nor dies.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes those who reach the imperishable state: free of pride, delusion, attachment and craving.

र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् ॥

nirmānamohā jitasaṅgadoṣā |

school_notes.note: Free of pride and delusion, having conquered attachment, always reflecting on the supreme self, with desires wholly gone, they reach that imperishable state.
Taking refuge in me, freed from the delusion of taking the non-self for the self and from attachment to the gunas' pleasures, devoted to meditation on the self, they reach it.
Gives a further means.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes his supreme abode, lit by no sun, moon or fire, from which there is no return.
devanagari:
न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः ।
यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥
iast:
na tadbhāsayate sūryo na śaśāṅko na pāvakaḥ |
yadgatvā na nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama ||
english: Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor fire lights it up; having gone there, people do not return. That is my supreme abode.

school_notes.note: Though the sun can illumine everything, it does not illumine that radiant state of Viṣṇu; neither do the moon or fire.
The light of the self is not lit by sun, moon or fire: knowledge itself reveals everything, while outer lights only remove the darkness between sense and object.
Describes the Lord's own nature.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says the individual self in every being is an eternal part of him.
devanagari:
ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः ।
मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति ॥

english: An eternal part of me, becoming a living being in the world of the living, draws to itself the senses, with the mind as the sixth, which rest in nature.

school_notes.note: A 'part' of me as the sun's reflection in water is a part of the sun: when the water is gone it returns to the sun; so the self, limited by adjuncts like space in a pot, is one with me.

The eternal self, truly a part of me, is covered by the ignorance of beginningless karma and so, as a living being, draws the senses in its body; another, freed of that ignorance, abides in its own form.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes the self carrying the senses from body to body as wind carries scents.
devanagari:
शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः ।
गृहीत्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात् ॥
iast:

school_notes.note: When the self, master of the body, leaves one body for another, it takes the senses with it, as wind carries scents from flowers.
As wind carries scents from garlands and sandalwood along with their fine particles, so the self, master of the senses, takes them with the subtle elements into its next body.
Rules out the soul's independence: it is the Lord who takes the senses along when the soul gains or leaves a body, as the Mokṣadharma says.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says the self experiences the world through the senses and the mind.

अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते ॥
iast:
śrotraṃ cakṣuḥ sparśanaṃ ca rasanaṃ ghrāṇameva ca |
adhiṣṭhāya manaścāyaṃ viṣayānupasevate ||
english: Presiding over hearing, sight, touch, taste and smell, and over the mind, it enjoys the objects of the senses.

school_notes.note: Dwelling in the body and presiding over each sense and the mind, it experiences sound and the other objects.
Directing the senses and the mind to their objects, the self enjoys sound and the rest.
The Lord too experiences through the senses, but only what is good, as the Upanishad says: 'evil does not reach the gods'.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says the deluded cannot see the self, while those with the eye of knowledge can.

english: Whether it is leaving the body, staying in it, or experiencing the world through the gunas, the deluded do not see it; those with the eye of knowledge see it.

school_notes.note: Though the self is so directly present, the deluded, drawn by pleasures seen and unseen, do not see it; those whose eye is knowledge, born of scripture, do.
Whether leaving a body, staying in it, or enjoying objects, the deluded never see the self as knowledge itself, distinct from the human body; those with the eye of knowledge do.
Answers why the Lord is not seen.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says striving yogis see the self within, but those who are not inwardly prepared do not, however hard they try.

यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः ॥

school_notes.note: Yogis who strive see the self in their own mind as 'I am this'; those not refined by austerity and self-mastery, who have not given up wrongdoing, do not see it even with the help of scripture.
Those who strive in karma yoga after taking refuge in me, minds purified, see the self as distinct from the body; those who strive without taking refuge in me do not.
'Not inwardly prepared' means of impure understanding.

context: Krishna begins describing how he sustains the world: the light of sun, moon and fire is his (15.12-15.15).

The radiance of the sun and the others, which lights the whole world, is mine, given to them by me when they worshipped me.
Expands the knowledge given earlier.

Entering the earth, I sustain all beings by my unhindered power; becoming the moon, full of nectar, I nourish all plants.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna distinguishes two kinds of person: the perishable and the imperishable (15.16-15.18).
devanagari:

The perishable is all beings, beginning with Brahmā; the unchanging imperishable is prakṛti; he cites a text naming the Lord as different from both.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says beyond both is the highest Person, the Supreme Self who sustains the three worlds.
devanagari:
उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः ।
यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः ॥

uttamaḥ puruṣastvanyaḥ paramātmetyudāhṛtaḥ |

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna explains why he is called the highest Person: he is beyond both the perishable and the imperishable.
devanagari:
यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः ।
अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
iast:
yasmātkṣaramatīto'hamakṣarādapi cottamaḥ |
ato'smi loke vede ca prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ ||
english: Because I am beyond the perishable and higher even than the imperishable, I am known in the world and in the Veda as the highest Person.

school_notes.note: Because I am beyond the perishable tree of worldly existence and higher than its seed, the imperishable, I am known as the highest Person.
Because I surpass the bound person and am higher even than the liberated one, I am known as the highest Person in scripture and in the traditions based on it.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says whoever knows him as the highest Person knows everything and worships him with their whole being.
devanagari:
यो मामेवमसंमूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम् ।
स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत ॥
iast:
yo māmevamasaṃmūḍho jānāti puruṣottamam |
sa sarvavidbhajati māṃ sarvabhāvena bhārata ||
english: Whoever, free of delusion, knows me in this way as the highest Person knows everything, and worships me with their whole being, Arjuna.

school_notes.note: Whoever knows me as 'I am this' knows everything and worships me, present in all beings, as the self of all.
Whoever knows me as different in kind from the perishable and imperishable persons knows all that must be known to reach me, and worships me in every way taught as a means to me.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna closes chapter 15, calling it the most secret teaching, which fulfils whoever understands it.
devanagari:
इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयानघ ।
एतद्‌बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत ॥
iast:
iti guhyatamaṃ śāstramidamuktaṃ mayānagha |
etadbuddhvā buddhimānsyātkṛtakṛtyaśca bhārata ||
english: So I have taught you this most secret teaching, sinless one. Understanding it, a person becomes wise and has done all there is to do, Arjuna.

school_notes.note: This chapter is called 'the teaching' in praise, since the whole meaning of the Gita, and indeed of the Vedas, is summed up in it.
This teaching that I am the highest Person is the most secret of all; understanding it, one has gained all the understanding and done all the duties that one who seeks me must.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna opens chapter 16 by listing the qualities of a divine nature (16.1-16.3).
devanagari:
अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिर्ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः ।
दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् ॥
iast:
abhayaṃ sattvasaṃśuddhirjñānayogavyavasthitiḥ |
dānaṃ damaśca yajñaśca svādhyāyastapa ārjavam ||
english: Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge, generosity, self-restraint, sacrifice, study of scripture, austerity, honesty,

school_notes.note: Fearlessness is freedom from fear; purity of heart means dealing with others without deceit, trickery or falsehood; steadfastness in knowledge is firm, focused understanding of the self gained from scripture and teacher.
Fear is the distress that comes from seeing a cause of losing the wanted or meeting the unwanted; fearlessness is its absence. Generosity is giving rightly earned wealth to a worthy recipient.
This chapter shows what opposes the means to life's goals; 'austerity' here means celibacy and the like.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna continues the divine qualities: non-violence, truth, freedom from anger, compassion and gentleness.
devanagari:
अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् ।
दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् ॥
iast:
ahiṃsā satyamakrodhastyāgaḥ śāntirapaiśunam |
dayā bhūteṣvaloluptvaṃ mārdavaṃ hrīracāpalam ||
english: non-violence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, renunciation, calm, not slandering others, compassion for all beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty and steadiness,

school_notes.note: Truth is saying what is so, without unkind falsehood; freedom from anger is calming anger that arises when one is abused or struck; not slandering is not exposing others' faults.

Freedom from anger is having no change of mind that leads to harming others; compassion is being unable to bear the suffering of any being; renunciation is letting go of possessions that work against one's true good.
Slander is telling a king or others of faults in order to bring trouble on someone; steadiness is not being fickle.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna completes the list of divine qualities, the inheritance of those born to a divine nature.
devanagari:
तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता ।
भवन्ति संपदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत ॥
iast:
tejaḥ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ śaucamadroho nātimānitā |
bhavanti saṃpadaṃ daivīmabhijātasya bhārata ||
english: vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from malice and from excessive pride: these belong to one born to the divine nature, Arjuna.

school_notes.note: Forgiveness is no inner disturbance arising when one is abused or struck, whereas freedom from anger is calming it once it has arisen; fortitude is what lifts body and senses when they sink.
Forgiveness is a mind unchanged towards others even when they cause one pain; fortitude is holding to what must be done even in great adversity.
Forgiveness is not harming one who has harmed you, together with freedom from anger.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna lists the qualities of a demonic nature: hypocrisy, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance.
devanagari:
दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च ।
अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ संपदमासुरीम् ॥
iast:
dambho darpo'bhimānaśca krodhaḥ pāruṣyameva ca |
ajñānaṃ cābhijātasya pārtha saṃpadamāsurīm ||
english: Hypocrisy, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance belong to one born to the demonic nature, son of Pritha.

school_notes.note: Hypocrisy is parading one's virtue; arrogance is pride in learning, wealth or family; harshness is cutting speech, such as calling a one-eyed man 'sharp-sighted'.
Hypocrisy is doing good to be known as good; harshness is a nature that troubles good people; ignorance is not discerning the higher and lower truths and what should and should not be done.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna reassures Arjuna that he was born to the divine nature, which leads to freedom.
devanagari:
दैवी संपद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता ।
मा शुचः संपदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव ॥
iast:
daivī saṃpadvimokṣāya nibandhāyāsurī matā |
mā śucaḥ saṃpadaṃ daivīmabhijāto'si pāṇḍava ||
english: The divine nature is thought to lead to liberation, the demonic to bondage. Do not grieve, son of Pandu: you are born to the divine nature.

school_notes.note: Seeing Arjuna wonder whether he has the demonic or the divine nature, Krishna tells him not to grieve: he is born to the divine.
The divine nature, following my command, leads step by step to me; the demonic, transgressing it, leads downward. Arjuna, frightened because he could not tell his own nature, is told not to grieve.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna introduces a fuller account of the demonic nature (16.6-16.20).
devanagari:
द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन्दैव आसुर एव च ।
दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे शृणु ॥
iast:
dvau bhūtasargau loke'smindaiva āsura eva ca |
daivo vistaraśaḥ prokta āsuraṃ pārtha me śṛṇu ||
english: There are two kinds of beings created in this world, the divine and the demonic. The divine has been described in detail; now hear from me about the demonic, son of Pritha.

school_notes.note: Humans are created with one of the two natures, divine or demonic, as the Upanishad says: 'the children of Prajāpati were of two kinds, gods and demons'.
By past merit and sin, beings are born from the start divided into those who follow the Lord's command and those who do the opposite.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says the demonic do not know what to do or avoid, and lack purity, good conduct and truth.
devanagari:
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः ।
न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते ॥
iast:
pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca janā na vidurāsurāḥ |
na śaucaṃ nāpi cācāro na satyaṃ teṣu vidyate ||
english: The demonic do not know what to take up and what to turn away from; there is no purity in them, no good conduct, and no truth.

school_notes.note: They know neither what to engage in for life's goals nor what to turn away from as harmful; and they have no purity, good conduct or truth.
They do not know the Vedic dharma that leads to prosperity and to liberation, nor the purity and conduct, such as the twilight prayer, that make one fit for it.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes the demonic worldview: a world without truth, foundation or God, driven only by desire.
devanagari:
असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम् ।
अपरस्परसंभूतं किमन्यत्कामहैतुकम् ॥
iast:
asatyamapratiṣṭhaṃ te jagadāhuranīśvaram |
aparasparasaṃbhūtaṃ kimanyatkāmahaitukam ||
english: They say the world is without truth, without foundation, without a Lord, not brought about by any order: what else is it but driven by desire?

school_notes.note: They say the world is unreal like themselves, has no basis in merit and demerit, and has no Lord who governs it by them; it is born of lust alone.
They do not say the world is the effect of Brahman, called 'the real', and rests in Brahman, upheld as the earth is by Ananta.
They deny the world's truth, foundation and Lord, all of which are Viṣṇu; he cites the Upanishad on the two forms of Brahman.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says those who hold this view become destructive, enemies of the world.
devanagari:
एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः ।
प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः ॥
iast:
etāṃ dṛṣṭimavaṣṭabhya naṣṭātmāno'lpabuddhayaḥ |
prabhavantyugrakarmāṇaḥ kṣayāya jagato'hitāḥ ||
english: Holding this view, these lost souls of small understanding and cruel deeds rise up as enemies of the world, for its destruction.

school_notes.note: Holding this view, having lost all means to the world beyond, with minds bent only on sense objects, they rise up as violent enemies of the world.
Not seeing a self beyond the body, unable to tell the knower from the body as known, they become violent towards all and rise up for the world's ruin.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes the demonic as driven by insatiable desire, hypocrisy, pride and arrogance.
devanagari:
काममाश्रित्य दुष्पूरं दम्भमानमदान्विताः ।
मोहाद्‌गृहीत्वासद्ग्राहान्प्रवर्तन्तेऽशुचिव्रताः ॥
iast:
kāmamāśritya duṣpūraṃ dambhamānamadānvitāḥ |
mohādgṛhītvāsadgrāhānpravartante'śucivratāḥ ||
english: Clinging to insatiable desire, full of hypocrisy, pride and arrogance, holding wrong ideas out of delusion, they act with impure intentions.

school_notes.note: Relying on desire that can never be filled, full of hypocrisy, pride and arrogance, they take up wrong resolves out of confusion and act on impure vows.
Pursuing hard-to-gain objects of desire, out of ignorance they take what is not theirs by wrong means and follow vows not prescribed by scripture.
Desire is hard to fill; he quotes the Mokṣadharma: 'like the netherworld, it can never be filled, and torments me always'.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes the endless anxieties of those who believe pleasure is everything.
devanagari:
चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः ।
कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्चिताः ॥
iast:
cintāmaparimeyāṃ ca pralayāntāmupāśritāḥ |
kāmopabhogaparamā etāvaditi niścitāḥ ||
english: Given over to boundless anxieties that end only with death, taking the enjoyment of desires as the highest aim, convinced that this is all there is,

school_notes.note: Their anxieties are beyond measure and end only with death; they hold that enjoying sense objects is the highest human goal.
Though they may die today or tomorrow, they take on endless worries about things that would take until the world's end to achieve, sure that enjoyment is the highest goal.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna continues: bound by countless hopes, they pile up wealth by unjust means.
devanagari:
आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः ।
ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान् ॥
iast:
āśāpāśaśatairbaddhāḥ kāmakrodhaparāyaṇāḥ |
īhante kāmabhogārthamanyāyenārthasañcayān ||
english: bound by hundreds of ropes of hope, given over to desire and anger, they strive to pile up wealth by unjust means to satisfy their desires.

school_notes.note: Bound by hundreds of nooses of hope, pulled every way, devoted to desire and anger, they seek wealth by unjust means such as taking what belongs to others, for pleasure, not for dharma.
Bound by hundreds of ropes of hope and wholly given to desire and anger, they strive to amass wealth unjustly for pleasure.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna voices the inner monologue of greed: always counting what was gained and what is next.
devanagari:
इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम् ।
इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम् ॥
iast:
idamadya mayā labdhamimaṃ prāpsye manoratham |
idamastīdamapi me bhaviṣyati punardhanam ||
english: "This I have gained today; this wish I will fulfil. This wealth is mine, and this too will be mine.

school_notes.note: 'I have gained this wealth today; I will gain that pleasing thing; next year more wealth will come and I will be known as rich.'
They think they gained land, children and wealth by their own power alone, not through unseen merit, and that they will gain more the same way.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna continues the monologue of arrogance: boasting of conquests and self-sufficiency.
devanagari:
असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि ।
ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी ॥
iast:
asau mayā hataḥ śatrurhaniṣye cāparānapi |
īśvaro'hamahaṃ bhogī siddho'haṃ balavānsukhī ||
english: That enemy has been killed by me, and I will kill others too. I am the lord, I am the enjoyer; I am successful, powerful and happy.

school_notes.note: 'I have killed that powerful enemy and will kill these wretches too; no one is my equal: I am lord, enjoyer, accomplished, strong and happy.'
They think: 'I killed my enemy by my own strength, and I need no help from unseen merit or a Lord; I am my own master and the master of others.'

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna completes the monologue of conceit and calls it the delusion of ignorance.
devanagari:
आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया ।
यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः ॥
iast:
āḍhyo'bhijanavānasmi ko'nyo'sti sadṛśo mayā |
yakṣye dāsyāmi modiṣya ityajñānavimohitāḥ ||
english: I am rich and well-born; who else is like me? I will sacrifice, I will give, I will rejoice." So they speak, deluded by ignorance.

school_notes.note: 'I am wealthy and of a learned family; who is equal to me? Even by sacrifice I will outdo others; I will give to performers and rejoice': so they think, confused by ignorance.
They think they can sacrifice and give by their own power alone, without the Lord's grace; this is the delusion of ignorance.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna warns where such delusion leads: confusion and a fall into hell.
devanagari:
अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः ।
प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ ॥
iast:
anekacittavibhrāntā mohajālasamāvṛtāḥ |
prasaktāḥ kāmabhogeṣu patanti narake'śucau ||
english: Bewildered by many thoughts, caught in the net of delusion, attached to the enjoyment of desires, they fall into a foul hell.

school_notes.note: Bewildered by many thoughts, covered by the net of delusion, clinging to pleasures and so heaping up sin, they fall into a foul hell such as Vaitaraṇī.
Thinking they can do everything without unseen merit or the Lord, they plan to do this and that, are caught in this net of delusion, and, dying in the midst of it, fall into a foul hell.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes the self-important who perform rituals only for show.
devanagari:
आत्मसंभाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः ।
यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् ॥
iast:
ātmasaṃbhāvitāḥ stabdhā dhanamānamadānvitāḥ |
yajante nāmayajñaiste dambhenāvidhipūrvakam ||
english: Self-important, stubborn, full of pride and the intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices in name only, out of hypocrisy, not according to the rules.

school_notes.note: Esteemed only by themselves, not by the good, unbending, they perform sacrifices that are sacrifices in name only, out of hypocrisy and without the prescribed parts.
Thinking well of themselves and intoxicated by wealth, learning and birth, they sacrifice only to be known as one who sacrifices.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says such people, driven by ego and anger, hate him who dwells in their own and others' bodies.
devanagari:
अहंकारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः ।
मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः ॥
iast:
ahaṃkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca saṃśritāḥ |
māmātmaparadeheṣu pradviṣanto'bhyasūyakāḥ ||
english: Given over to ego, force, arrogance, desire and anger, these resentful people hate me, who dwell in their own bodies and in those of others.

school_notes.note: Ego is thinking oneself special through virtues one has or does not have; it is ignorance, the root of all faults and all harmful action.
Relying on the ego that thinks 'I alone do everything', on their own strength, pride and desire, and on anger against all who oppose them, they hate me, who dwell within them and others.
They say, 'Viṣṇu makes no one act; if he did, let him make me act now'; he cites a Sāmaveda text that such a person goes downward.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says he casts those who hate and harm into repeated births of a demonic kind (16.19-16.20).
devanagari:
तानहं द्विषतः क्रुरान्संसारेषु नराधमान् ।
क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु ॥
iast:
tānahaṃ dviṣataḥ krurānsaṃsāreṣu narādhamān |
kṣipāmyajasramaśubhānāsurīṣveva yoniṣu ||
english: These hateful, cruel, vilest of people, I hurl again and again into the cycles of rebirth, into demonic wombs alone.

school_notes.note: Those who hate the good and hate me I cast again and again into cruel births such as those of tigers and lions.
Those who hate me I cast into births hostile to me, and into the cruel states of mind that lead to such births.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says the deluded fall lower with each birth, never reaching him.
devanagari:
आसुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि ।
मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम् ॥
iast:
āsurīṃ yonimāpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani |
māmaprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yāntyadhamāṃ gatim ||
english: Falling into demonic wombs, deluded birth after birth, never reaching me, son of Kunti, they sink to the lowest state.

school_notes.note: Born in such wombs again and again, sinking lower, they go to an even lower state; 'never reaching me' does not imply they ever could have.
Born again and again in births hostile to me, never gaining the knowledge that the Lord Vāsudeva exists, they go lower and lower.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna names the three gates to hell, desire, anger and greed, and urges giving them up.
devanagari:
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः ।
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥
iast:
trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ |
kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet ||
english: Threefold is this gate of hell that destroys the self: desire, anger and greed. So one should give up these three.

school_notes.note: Entering this gate, the self is ruined and becomes unfit for any of life's goals; so give up desire, anger and greed.
Desire, anger and greed are the path into this demonic nature, which is a hell; since they lead to terrible hell, give them up from far off.

Sattvic faith leads to worship that brings happiness unmixed with sorrow; rajasic faith gives small pleasure mixed with sorrow; tamasic faith gives even less.

Renunciation is setting aside desire-driven rites, either by not wanting their fruit or by not doing them; relinquishment is giving up the fruit, as a Sāmaveda text says.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says one free of the sense of doership and untainted is not bound, even in killing; the words are spoken on the battlefield.
devanagari:
यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते ।
हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते ॥
iast:
yasya nāhaṃkṛto bhāvo buddhiryasya na lipyate |
hatvāpi sa imām̐llokānna hanti na nibadhyate ||
english: One who is free of the sense of 'I am the doer', whose understanding is not tainted, even if they kill these people, does not kill and is not bound.

school_notes.note: One refined by scripture, teacher and reasoning, who knows 'the five factors act, I am only their witness', is not tainted, and even killing, does not kill.
One who, reflecting that the Supreme Person is the doer, has no thought 'I am doing this', and whose understanding is not tainted by thinking the fruit is theirs, is not bound.
Praises this knowledge; one who still has a slight sense of doership is slightly bound.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna names the components that prompt and make up action (18.18-18.19).
devanagari:
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना ।
करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसंग्रहः ॥
iast:
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ parijñātā trividhā karmacodanā |
karaṇaṃ karma karteti trividhaḥ karmasaṃgrahaḥ ||
english: Knowledge, the object of knowledge and the knower are the threefold impulse to action; the instrument, the action and the doer are the threefold basis of action.

school_notes.note: Knowledge, the known and the knower together prompt all action; instrument, action and doer are where action rests.
The Vedic injunction to act involves knowledge of the duty, the duty to be known, and the one who knows it; the duty itself is made up of instrument, action and doer.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says knowledge, action and the doer each come in three kinds according to the gunas (18.19-18.28).
devanagari:
ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः ।
प्रोच्यते गुणसंख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि ॥
iast:
jñānaṃ karma ca kartā ca tridhaiva guṇabhedataḥ |
procyate guṇasaṃkhyāne yathāvacchṛṇu tānyapi ||
english: Knowledge, action and the doer are said, in the account of the gunas, to be of three kinds each, according to the gunas. Hear about these as they are.

school_notes.note: Each of these is of three kinds, by the difference of sattva and the rest; 'only' shows there is no class apart from the gunas.
Knowledge of the duty, the duty performed and the one who performs it are each threefold by the gunas.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes sattvic knowledge: seeing the one imperishable reality in all beings.
devanagari:
सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते ।
अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम् ॥
iast:
sarvabhūteṣu yenaikaṃ bhāvamavyayamīkṣate |
avibhaktaṃ vibhakteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi sāttvikam ||
english: The knowledge by which one sees in all beings one imperishable reality, undivided among the divided, know that knowledge to be sattvic.

school_notes.note: The knowledge that sees one self, unchanging, in all beings from the unmanifest to plants, undivided like space in all bodies, is sattvic.
The knowledge that sees, in beings divided by role and stage of life, one self of the nature of knowledge, undivided, is sattvic.
The one reality is Viṣṇu.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes rajasic knowledge: seeing beings as wholly separate, each a different kind.
devanagari:
पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान् ।
वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम् ॥
iast:
pṛthaktvena tu yajjñānaṃ nānābhāvānpṛthagvidhān |
vetti sarveṣu bhūteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi rājasam ||
english: But the knowledge that sees in all beings many separate realities, of different kinds, each apart from the others, know that knowledge to be rajasic.

school_notes.note: The knowledge that takes each body's self to be different, with different characteristics, is rajasic.
The knowledge that takes selves to be as different as the bodies they inhabit, white or tall, and so fit for different rewards, is rajasic.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes tamasic knowledge: clinging to one small thing as if it were everything.
devanagari:
यत्तु कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन्कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम् ।
अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
iast:
yattu kṛtsnavadekasminkārye saktamahaitukam |
atattvārthavadalpaṃ ca tattāmasamudāhṛtam ||
english: But the knowledge that clings to one single thing as if it were the whole, without reason, missing the truth and narrow, is called tamasic.

school_notes.note: Knowledge that clings to one effect, such as the body or an image, as if it were everything, as the naked ascetics take the self to be body-sized, is tamasic.
Knowledge attached to one trifling act, such as worship of ghosts and spirits, as if it brought every reward, without real basis and missing the truth, is tamasic.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes sattvic action: done as duty, without attachment, attraction, aversion or desire for reward.
devanagari:
नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् ।
अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते ॥
iast:
niyataṃ saṅgarahitamarāgadveṣataḥ kṛtam |
aphalaprepsunā karma yattatsāttvikamucyate ||
english: Action that is prescribed, done without attachment, without attraction or aversion, by one who does not crave its fruit, is called sattvic.

school_notes.note: Regular action, without attachment, not done from attraction or aversion, by one who does not thirst for the fruit, is sattvic.
Action suited to one's station, free of attachment to doership, not done from love of fame or fear of disgrace, without seeking fruit, is sattvic.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes rajasic action: done with great strain, for desires, or with ego.
devanagari:
यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहंकारेण वा पुनः ।
क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् ॥
iast:
yattu kāmepsunā karma sāhaṃkāreṇa vā punaḥ |
kriyate bahulāyāsaṃ tadrājasamudāhṛtam ||
english: But action done by one who craves desires, or with ego, with great strain, is called rajasic.

school_notes.note: 'With ego' is said in contrast to ordinary people without vanity, not to the knower of truth, who never acts craving desires or with great strain.
Action done for its fruit and with the conceit 'I alone am doing this great labour' is rajasic.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes tamasic action: begun in delusion, heedless of consequences, loss, harm or one's own capacity.
devanagari:
अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनवेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् ।
मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते ॥
iast:
anubandhaṃ kṣayaṃ hiṃsāmanavekṣya ca pauruṣam |
mohādārabhyate karma yattattāmasamucyate ||
english: Action undertaken out of delusion, without regard to consequences, loss, harm to others, or one's own capacity, is called tamasic.

school_notes.note: Action begun without regard to its consequences, to the loss of strength or wealth it causes, to harm to living beings, or to whether one can finish it, is tamasic.
Action begun without weighing the suffering that follows, the loss of wealth, harm to beings, or one's ability to finish it, out of not knowing that the Supreme Person is the doer, is tamasic.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes the sattvic doer: unattached, steady, enthusiastic and unmoved by success or failure.
devanagari:
मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः ।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥
iast:
muktasaṅgo'nahaṃvādī dhṛtyutsāhasamanvitaḥ |
siddhyasiddhyornirvikāraḥ kartā sāttvika ucyate ||
english: A doer who is free of attachment, does not talk of 'I', is full of steadiness and enthusiasm, and is unchanged by success and failure, is called sattvic.

school_notes.note: Free of attachment, not given to saying 'I', with steadiness and zeal, unchanged whether the work succeeds or fails: such a doer is sattvic.
Steadiness is bearing the unavoidable hardships until the work is done; enthusiasm is an eager mind; such a doer is unchanged by victory or defeat in tasks such as battle.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes the rajasic doer: passionate, greedy, harmful, impure and swept by joy and grief.
devanagari:
रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः ।
हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः ॥
iast:
rāgī karmaphalaprepsurlubdho hiṃsātmako'śuciḥ |
harṣaśokānvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ ||
english: A doer who is passionate, craves the fruits of action, is greedy, harmful and impure, and is swept by joy and grief, is called rajasic.

school_notes.note: Passionate, wanting fruits, greedy for others' wealth or unwilling to give one's own, harmful to others, impure, and swayed by joy and grief: such a doer is rajasic.
Seeking fame and fruits, unwilling to spend what the work needs, getting work done by harming others, and elated or downcast by victory or defeat.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes the tamasic doer: undisciplined, stubborn, deceitful, lazy, despondent and procrastinating.
devanagari:
अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः ।
विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥
iast:
ayuktaḥ prākṛtaḥ stabdhaḥ śaṭho naiṣkṛtiko'lasaḥ |
viṣādī dīrghasūtrī ca kartā tāmasa ucyate ||
english: A doer who is undisciplined, coarse, stubborn, deceitful, malicious, lazy, despondent and procrastinating is called tamasic.

school_notes.note: Undisciplined, unrefined like a child, unbending, deceitful, divisive, idle even in what must be done, always despondent, and procrastinating: such a doer is tamasic.
Unfit for scriptural action, untaught, slow to begin, drawn to harmful rites, deceitful, sluggish even in work begun, easily discouraged, and slow to finish.
Reads 'dīrghasūtrī' not as procrastinating but as one who keeps bringing up another's old faults.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna turns to understanding and fortitude, each of three kinds according to the gunas (18.29-18.35).
devanagari:
बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं शृणु ।
प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनंजय ॥
iast:
buddherbhedaṃ dhṛteścaiva guṇatastrividhaṃ śṛṇu |
procyamānamaśeṣeṇa pṛthaktvena dhanaṃjaya ||
english: Now hear, Arjuna, the threefold division of understanding and of fortitude according to the gunas, explained fully and separately.

school_notes.note: Hear the threefold difference of understanding and fortitude by the gunas; Arjuna is called Dhanañjaya because he won great wealth in his conquests.
Understanding is discerning, decisive knowledge; fortitude is the power to hold to a task once begun despite obstacles.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes sattvic understanding: knowing what to do and avoid, what binds and what frees.
devanagari:
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये ।
बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥
iast:
pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca kāryākārye bhayābhaye |
bandhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī ||
english: The understanding that knows when to act and when to refrain, what should and should not be done, what is to be feared and what is not, and what binds and what frees, son of Pritha, is sattvic.

school_notes.note: Engagement is the path of action, which binds; withdrawal is the path of renunciation, which frees; sattvic understanding knows these, what to do and avoid, and what to fear and not.
Engagement is dharma that brings prosperity; withdrawal is dharma that brings liberation; sattvic understanding knows both and what is to be done in each place, time and situation.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes rajasic understanding: unable to tell right from wrong clearly.
devanagari:
यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च ।
अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥
iast:
yayā dharmamadharmaṃ ca kāryaṃ cākāryameva ca |
ayathāvatprajānāti buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī ||
english: The understanding by which one knows wrongly what is dharma and what is not, what should and should not be done, son of Pritha, is rajasic.

school_notes.note: Understanding that does not decide rightly between what scripture enjoins and forbids, or what is to be done and avoided, is rajasic.
Understanding that does not rightly know the two kinds of dharma and their opposites, or what is to be done in each situation, is rajasic.
Rajasic understanding is not reliably correct; if it were always wrong, it would not differ from tamasic understanding.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes tamasic understanding: covered in darkness, it takes wrong for right and sees everything backwards.
devanagari:
अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसावृता ।
सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥
iast:
adharmaṃ dharmamiti yā manyate tamasāvṛtā |
sarvārthānviparītāṃśca buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī ||
english: The understanding which, covered by darkness, takes adharma for dharma and sees all things in reverse, son of Pritha, is tamasic.

school_notes.note: Understanding covered by tamas takes the forbidden to be enjoined and sees everything knowable the wrong way round.
Tamasic understanding thinks adharma is dharma and dharma adharma, the real unreal and the unreal real, the highest lower and the lower highest.
