speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes sattvic fortitude: unwavering steadiness that governs mind, breath and senses through yoga.
devanagari:
धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः ।
योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥
iast:
dhṛtyā yayā dhārayate manaḥprāṇendriyakriyāḥ |
yogenāvyabhicāriṇyā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī ||
english: The unwavering fortitude by which, through yoga, one controls the activities of mind, breath and senses, son of Pritha, is sattvic.

school_notes.note: The fortitude that, never wavering, holds the mind, breath and senses back from going against scripture is sattvic.
Yoga here is worship of the Lord as the means to liberation; the fortitude that keeps mind, breath and senses directed to that goal is sattvic.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes rajasic fortitude: holding to dharma, pleasure and wealth for the sake of their rewards.
devanagari:
यया तु धर्मकामार्थान्धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन ।
प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥
iast:
yayā tu dharmakāmārthāndhṛtyā dhārayate'rjuna |
prasaṅgena phalākāṅkṣī dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī ||
english: But the fortitude by which one holds to dharma, pleasure and wealth, Arjuna, craving their fruits out of attachment, son of Pritha, is rajasic.

school_notes.note: The fortitude by which one holds dharma, pleasure and wealth always in mind as things to pursue, wanting their fruit in each case, is rajasic.
The fortitude by which one seeking fruits, out of strong attachment, keeps the mind and senses set on dharma, pleasure and wealth is rajasic.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes tamasic fortitude: stubbornly clinging to sleep, fear, grief, despondency and arrogance.
devanagari:
यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च ।
न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥
iast:
yayā svapnaṃ bhayaṃ śokaṃ viṣādaṃ madameva ca |
na vimuñcati durmedhā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī ||
english: The fortitude by which a foolish person does not let go of sleep, fear, grief, despondency and arrogance, son of Pritha, is tamasic.

school_notes.note: The fortitude of a foolish person who keeps holding on to sleep, fear, grief, despondency and the intoxication of pleasures, as if they were duties, is tamasic.
The fortitude by which the foolish keep the mind and senses fixed on sleep and on the intoxication of pleasures, and on the things that bring fear, grief and despondency, is tamasic.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna turns to happiness, which is also of three kinds (18.36-18.39).
devanagari:
सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं शृणु मे भरतर्षभ ।
अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति ॥
iast:
sukhaṃ tvidānīṃ trividhaṃ śṛṇu me bharatarṣabha |
abhyāsādramate yatra duḥkhāntaṃ ca nigacchati ||
english: Now hear from me, best of the Bharatas, about the three kinds of happiness: the happiness one comes to enjoy through practice, in which sorrow comes to an end,

school_notes.note: Hear the three kinds of happiness: that which one comes to delight in through practice, and in which one surely reaches the end of sorrow.
All the knowledge, action and doers described serve happiness, which is also threefold; in the highest, long practice brings complete delight and the end of all worldly sorrow.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes sattvic happiness: like poison at first but like nectar in the end.
devanagari:
यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् ।
तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥
iast:
yattadagre viṣamiva pariṇāme'mṛtopamam |
tatsukhaṃ sāttvikaṃ proktamātmabuddhiprasādajam ||
english: That which is like poison at first but like nectar in the end, born of the clarity of one's own understanding, is called sattvic happiness.

school_notes.note: At first, when knowledge, dispassion and meditation begin, it is like poison because of the great effort; when they ripen, it is like nectar; it is born of a clear understanding of the self.
At the start of yoga it feels like poison, being hard work and the self not yet experienced; as practice ripens and the self shines forth, it becomes like nectar.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes rajasic happiness: like nectar at first but like poison in the end.
devanagari:
विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् ।
परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥
iast:
viṣayendriyasaṃyogādyattadagre'mṛtopamam |
pariṇāme viṣamiva tatsukhaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam ||
english: That which arises from the contact of the senses with their objects, like nectar at first but like poison in the end, is held to be rajasic happiness.

school_notes.note: Pleasure from contact of senses and objects is like nectar at first but like poison in the end, since it wastes strength, vigour, beauty, wisdom and wealth and leads to wrongdoing.
While enjoyed it seems like nectar; but once the hunger that made it pleasant is gone, and since it leads to hell and the like, it turns out like poison drunk.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes tamasic happiness: deluding from beginning to end, born of sleep, sloth and carelessness.
devanagari:
यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः ।
निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
iast:
yadagre cānubandhe ca sukhaṃ mohanamātmanaḥ |
nidrālasyapramādotthaṃ tattāmasamudāhṛtam ||
english: The happiness that deludes the self both at first and in the end, arising from sleep, laziness and carelessness, is called tamasic.

school_notes.note: Happiness that confuses the self at the start and afterwards, arising from sleep, laziness and carelessness, is tamasic.
Happiness that clouds true knowledge both while enjoyed and afterwards, arising from sleep, laziness and carelessness, is tamasic.

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says no being anywhere is free of the three gunas.
devanagari:
न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः ।
सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्त्रिभिर्गुणैः ॥
iast:
na tadasti pṛthivyāṃ vā divi deveṣu vā punaḥ |
sattvaṃ prakṛtijairmuktaṃ yadebhiḥ syāttribhirguṇaiḥ ||
english: There is no being on earth, or in heaven among the gods, that is free of these three gunas born of nature.

school_notes.note: No being, among humans on earth or gods in heaven, living or not, is free of these three gunas born of nature.
No being bound up with prakṛti, from Brahmā down to plants, on earth or in heaven, is free of these three gunas.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says the duties of the four varnas are divided according to the gunas of each one's nature (18.41-18.48).
devanagari:
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परन्तप ।
कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः ॥
iast:
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca parantapa |
karmāṇi pravibhaktāni svabhāvaprabhavairguṇaiḥ ||
english: The duties of brahmins, kshatriyas and vaishyas, and of shudras too, Arjuna, are divided according to the gunas that arise from their own nature.

school_notes.note: Shudras are named outside the compound because, though also a class, they are not entitled to the Veda; the duties are divided from one another by the gunas that arise from nature.
'Nature' here is the past karma that causes birth as a brahmin and so on; from it arise the gunas, with sattva dominant over rajas and tamas in the brahmin.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna lists the qualities he describes as the natural work of a brahmin.
devanagari:
शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च ।
ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम् ॥
iast:
śamo damastapaḥ śaucaṃ kṣāntirārjavameva ca |
jñānaṃ vijñānamāstikyaṃ brahmakarma svabhāvajam ||
english: Calm, self-restraint, austerity, purity, patience, honesty, knowledge, insight and faith are the work of a brahmin, born of their nature.

school_notes.note: Calm and self-restraint are as explained before; faith means trust in the teaching of scripture; these are the duties of the brahmin class, born of their nature.
Calm restrains the outer senses and self-restraint the mind; patience is an unshaken mind even when others cause pain; honesty is showing outwardly what is in one's mind.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna lists the qualities he describes as the natural work of a kshatriya, including not fleeing from battle.
devanagari:
शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् ।
दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम् ॥
iast:
śauryaṃ tejo dhṛtirdākṣyaṃ yuddhe cāpyapalāyanam |
dānamīśvarabhāvaśca kṣātraṃ karma svabhāvajam ||
english: Courage, vigour, steadiness, skill, not fleeing in battle, generosity and leadership are the work of a kshatriya, born of their nature.

school_notes.note: Steadiness keeps one from sinking in any situation; skill is acting without confusion when tasks arise suddenly; and one does not turn away in battle.
Courage is the ability to enter battle fearlessly; steadiness is finishing a task despite obstacles; not fleeing means not turning back even when sure of one's own death.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna names farming, cattle-keeping and trade as the vaishya's natural work, and service as the shudra's.
devanagari:
कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम् ।
परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम् ॥
iast:
kṛṣigaurakṣyavāṇijyaṃ vaiśyakarma svabhāvajam |
paricaryātmakaṃ karma śūdrasyāpi svabhāvajam ||
english: Farming, tending cattle and trade are the work of a vaishya, born of their nature; and work that consists of service is the shudra's, also born of their nature.

school_notes.note: Farming is tilling the land, tending cattle is herding, and trade is buying and selling; these are the vaishya's work.
Trade is buying and selling to accumulate wealth; the shudra's natural work is service to the three preceding varnas.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says each person reaches perfection by devotion to their own work, and promises to explain how.
devanagari:
स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः ।
स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥
iast:
sve sve karmaṇyabhirataḥ saṃsiddhiṃ labhate naraḥ |
svakarmanirataḥ siddhiṃ yathā vindati tacchṛṇu ||
english: Each devoted to their own work, a person attains perfection. Hear how one devoted to their own work finds perfection.

school_notes.note: The perfection meant is fitness of body and senses for steadfastness in knowledge, once impurity has been worn away by doing one's own duties.
Devoted to their own work as described, a person attains perfection, meaning the highest state.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says one reaches perfection by worshipping, through one's own work, the source of all beings.
devanagari:
यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।
स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥
iast:
yataḥ pravṛttirbhūtānāṃ yena sarvamidaṃ tatam |
svakarmaṇā tamabhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ ||
english: By worshipping, through their own work, the one from whom all beings arise and by whom all this is pervaded, a person attains perfection.

school_notes.note: Beings arise from the Lord, the inner controller, who pervades the world; worshipping him through the duty of one's varna, one gains perfection.
Worshipping me, present as the inner self of Indra and the other gods, through one's own work, one gains by my grace the perfection of reaching me.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna repeats that one's own dharma, though imperfect, is better than another's well performed (compare 3.35).
devanagari:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।
स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
iast:
śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt |
svabhāvaniyataṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam ||
english: Better one's own dharma, though imperfect, than another's dharma well performed. Doing the work set by one's own nature, one incurs no fault.

school_notes.note: One's own duty is better even when lacking; as poison does not harm the worm born in it, work set by one's nature brings no sin.

One's own dharma here is karma yoga as worship of me, which comes easily to one bound up with nature; even imperfect, it is better than the path of knowledge suited to those who have mastered the senses.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says one should not give up the work one is born to, since every undertaking has some fault.
devanagari:
सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् ।
सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥
iast:
sahajaṃ karma kaunteya sadoṣamapi na tyajet |
sarvārambhā hi doṣeṇa dhūmenāgnirivāvṛtāḥ ||
english: Do not give up the work you were born to, son of Kunti, even if it has faults; for all undertakings are clouded by fault, as fire is by smoke.

school_notes.note: Work one is born with should not be abandoned even though faulty, being made of the three gunas; every undertaking, one's own duty or another's, is covered by fault.

Because it is natural, easy and less prone to error, do not give it up even if painful; even one fit for the path of knowledge should practise karma yoga, since every undertaking, of action or knowledge, carries pain like smoke.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna begins describing how one reaches the highest state: through non-attachment and renunciation (18.49-18.55).
devanagari:
असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः ।
नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति ॥
iast:
asaktabuddhiḥ sarvatra jitātmā vigataspṛhaḥ |
naiṣkarmyasiddhiṃ paramāṃ saṃnyāsenādhigacchati ||
english: One whose understanding is unattached everywhere, who has mastered themselves and is free of craving, reaches through renunciation the supreme perfection of freedom from action.

school_notes.note: Unattached to son, wife and other occasions of attachment, with the mind mastered, and free of craving for body, life and pleasures.

Unattached to fruits, and free of desire for one's own doership by reflecting that the Supreme Person is the doer, one who acts with renunciation (understood as relinquishment) reaches the highest perfection, the culmination of meditation.
The perfection of freedom from action is the perfection of yoga whose fruit is freedom from action.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna promises to explain briefly how one who has reached perfection attains Brahman.
devanagari:
सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे ।
समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा ॥
iast:
siddhiṃ prāpto yathā brahma tathāpnoti nibodha me |
samāsenaiva kaunteya niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā ||
english: Learn from me briefly, son of Kunti, how one who has reached perfection attains Brahman, which is the highest culmination of knowledge.

school_notes.note: The perfection reached is fitness of body and senses for steadfastness in knowledge, born of the Lord's grace after worshipping him through one's own work.
Having reached the perfection of meditation produced by karma yoga practised daily until death; 'the highest culmination of knowledge' further describes Brahman.
Learn the means by which one who has reached perfection attains Brahman; that perfection is the highest culmination of knowledge.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna describes the discipline that leads to Brahman: purified understanding, self-control and letting go of likes and dislikes (18.51-18.53).
devanagari:
बुद्ध्या विशुद्ध्या युक्तो धृत्यात्मानं नियम्य च ।
शब्दादीन्विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च ॥
iast:
buddhyā viśuddhyā yukto dhṛtyātmānaṃ niyamya ca |
śabdādīnviṣayāṃstyaktvā rāgadveṣau vyudasya ca ||
english: Endowed with a purified understanding, controlling oneself with steadiness, turning away from sound and the other objects of the senses, and casting aside attraction and aversion,

school_notes.note: With an understanding free of illusion, controlling body and senses with fortitude, and giving up sense objects except those needed only to sustain the body.

With understanding of the self as it truly is, making the mind fit for yoga by turning it from objects, keeping sense objects at a distance and casting off the attraction and aversion they cause, and living in solitude.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna continues: living in solitude, eating lightly and practising meditation with dispassion.
devanagari:
विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः ।
ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः ॥
iast:
viviktasevī laghvāśī yatavākkāyamānasaḥ |
dhyānayogaparo nityaṃ vairāgyaṃ samupāśritaḥ ||
english: living in solitude, eating lightly, with speech, body and mind controlled, always intent on the yoga of meditation, taking refuge in dispassion,

school_notes.note: Given to frequenting solitary places such as forests, riverbanks and mountain caves, and to eating lightly; both remove faults such as sleepiness and bring clarity of mind.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna completes the description: free of ego, desire, anger and possessions, one becomes fit for Brahman.
devanagari:
अहंकारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् ।
विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
iast:
ahaṃkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigraham |
vimucya nirmamaḥ śānto brahmabhūyāya kalpate ||
english: letting go of ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessions, free of the sense of 'mine' and at peace, one becomes fit to attain the state of Brahman.

school_notes.note: 'Force' means strength joined with desire and passion, not bodily strength, which being natural cannot be given up; arrogance follows elation and leads one to transgress dharma.
The state of Brahman means abiding in Brahman: having the mind always fixed on it.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says one who has attained the state of Brahman is serene, free of grief and craving, and gains supreme devotion.
devanagari:
ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् ॥
iast:
brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati |
samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu madbhaktiṃ labhate parām ||
english: Having attained the state of Brahman, serene within, one neither grieves nor craves; equal towards all beings, one gains supreme devotion to me.

school_notes.note: Such a person does not grieve over any lack or any failing of their own, and does not crave, since craving for what is not yet gained is impossible for a knower of Brahman.
One whose self is revealed as unlimited knowledge, wholly subordinate to me (as in 7.5), untainted by afflictions and karma, and regarding no being as other than mine.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says through devotion one comes to know him truly and then enters into him.
devanagari:
भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः ।
ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ॥
iast:
bhaktyā māmabhijānāti yāvānyaścāsmi tattvataḥ |
tato māṃ tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram ||
english: Through devotion one comes to know me truly, how great I am and who I am; then, having known me truly, one enters into me.

school_notes.note: One knows me both as I appear spread out through limiting adjuncts and as I truly am, free of them: non-dual pure consciousness, ageless, fearless and deathless.
One knows me as I am in essence, nature, qualities and glories; after that knowledge, through devotion, one enters into me.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says even one fully engaged in action, if relying on him, reaches the eternal state by his grace.
devanagari:
सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः ।
मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ॥
iast:
sarvakarmāṇyapi sadā kurvāṇo madvyapāśrayaḥ |
matprasādādavāpnoti śāśvataṃ padamavyayam ||
english: Even while always doing all kinds of action, one who takes refuge in me reaches, by my grace, the eternal, imperishable state.

school_notes.note: Reads 'all actions' as including even prohibited ones: one who has offered their whole being to me, Vāsudeva, reaches the eternal state by the Lord's grace.
Not only regular and occasional duties but even desire-driven acts, done by one who has placed doership and the rest in me, lead by my grace to the eternal state, which is reaching me.
Having again stated the inner means, Krishna concludes.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all his actions to him and keep his mind always on him.
devanagari:
चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः ।
बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव ॥
iast:
cetasā sarvakarmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparaḥ |
buddhiyogamupāśritya maccittaḥ satataṃ bhava ||
english: Mentally offering all actions to me, holding me as the highest, relying on the yoga of understanding, keep your mind always on me.

school_notes.note: With a discerning mind, offer all actions to me as taught in 9.27, and resort to the yoga of understanding, a concentrated mind.
Knowing the self belongs to me and is governed by me, as in 3.30, place all actions, with their doership and the one worshipped, in me, regarding me alone as the goal.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna tells Arjuna that with his mind on Krishna he will overcome every difficulty, but ego that refuses to listen will ruin him.
devanagari:
मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि ।
अथ चेत्त्वमहंकारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि ॥
iast:
maccittaḥ sarvadurgāṇi matprasādāttariṣyasi |
atha cettvamahaṃkārānna śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi ||
english: With your mind on me, you will cross every difficulty by my grace; but if out of ego you will not listen, you will be lost.

school_notes.note: You will cross all the hard-to-cross causes of worldly life; but if, thinking 'I am learned', you do not heed my words, you will come to ruin.
If, thinking 'I alone know what should and should not be done', you do not listen to me, you will be lost.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: On the battlefield, Krishna tells Arjuna that his refusal to fight is futile, because his own nature will drive him to it.
devanagari:
यदहंकारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे ।
मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति ॥
iast:
yadahaṃkāramāśritya na yotsya iti manyase |
mithyaiṣa vyavasāyaste prakṛtistvāṃ niyokṣyati ||
english: If, relying on ego, you think 'I will not fight', that resolve of yours is in vain: your own nature will compel you.

school_notes.note: Your resolve not to fight is false, because your nature, the temperament of a kshatriya, will drive you.
Ego here is presuming to be independent in knowing what is good for oneself and disregarding my command; that resolve will fail, because your nature will drive you into battle.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna adds that Arjuna's warrior nature will make him do the fighting he now refuses out of confusion.
devanagari:
स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा ।
कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत् ॥
iast:
svabhāvajena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā |
kartuṃ necchasi yanmohātkariṣyasyavaśo'pi tat ||
english: Bound by your own action, born of your nature, son of Kunti, what you do not wish to do out of delusion you will do, even against your will.

school_notes.note: Bound by your own action, such as the courage described earlier, you will do that work helplessly, under another's control, though from lack of discernment you do not want to.

Courage is the kshatriya's natural work; bound by it and unable to bear being overpowered by enemies, you yourself will fight the battle you now refuse out of ignorance; all beings are governed by me, the Lord of all.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says the Lord dwells in the heart of every being and moves all beings by his power.
devanagari:
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति ।
भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥
iast:
īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛddeśe'rjuna tiṣṭhati |
bhrāmayansarvabhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā ||
english: The Lord dwells in the heart of all beings, Arjuna, making all beings turn by his power, as if they were mounted on a machine.

school_notes.note: The Lord, Nārāyaṇa, dwells in the region of the heart; 'Arjuna' (white) here signals one of pure mind, citing the Ṛgveda; he makes beings revolve by māyā.
Vāsudeva, the controller of all, dwells in the heart, where the knowledge behind all action and restraint arises, moving beings mounted on the machine of body and senses that he himself made.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna urges Arjuna to take refuge in the Lord with his whole being, promising peace and the eternal abode.
devanagari:
तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत ।
तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥
iast:
tameva śaraṇaṃ gaccha sarvabhāvena bhārata |
tatprasādātparāṃ śāntiṃ sthānaṃ prāpsyasi śāśvatam ||
english: Take refuge in him alone with your whole being, Arjuna; by his grace you will reach supreme peace and the eternal abode.

school_notes.note: Take refuge in the Lord wholeheartedly to remove the pain of worldly life; by his grace you will gain supreme peace and my, Viṣṇu's, highest state.
Take refuge in me, the ruler of all, who out of love for those who depend on me stands as your charioteer, and follow my instruction 'do this'.
Krishna speaks of himself in the third person, as Bhīma does when speaking to Droṇa.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Having finished his teaching, Krishna invites Arjuna to reflect on it fully and then choose for himself.
devanagari:
इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्‌गुह्यतरं मया ।
विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
iast:
iti te jñānamākhyātaṃ guhyādguhyataraṃ mayā |
vimṛśyaitadaśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru ||
english: Thus I have taught you wisdom more secret than all secrets. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you choose.

school_notes.note: This most secret knowledge has been told by me, the all-knowing Lord; having reflected on the whole teaching, do as you wish.
All the knowledge seekers of liberation need, of karma yoga, the path of knowledge and bhakti yoga, has been told; reflecting on it, follow whichever suits your fitness.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says he will repeat his most secret, highest teaching because Arjuna is dearly loved.
devanagari:
सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः शृणु मे परमं वचः ।
इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥
iast:
sarvaguhyatamaṃ bhūyaḥ śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ |
iṣṭo'si me dṛḍhamiti tato vakṣyāmi te hitam ||
english: Hear once more my supreme word, the most secret of all. You are dearly loved by me, so I will tell you what is for your good.

school_notes.note: Hear again my supreme word, though often said; I speak not from fear or for gain but because you are firmly dear to me.
Bhakti yoga, being the best, was already called most secret (9.1); hear again my supreme word about it.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna gives his most secret teaching: devotion to him, with the promise that Arjuna will come to him.
devanagari:
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।
मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥
iast:
manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru |
māmevaiṣyasi satyaṃ te pratijāne priyo'si me ||
english: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, worship me, bow down to me. You will come to me; I promise you truly, for you are dear to me.

school_notes.note: Keep your mind on me, worship me, and offer even your salutation to me alone; living thus, with means, end and purpose offered to Vāsudeva, you will come to me; I promise this truly.

Citing Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 3.8 ('knowing him thus, one becomes immortal here; there is no other path'), the knowing, meditation and worship enjoined there is a continuous remembrance as vivid as seeing.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna's culminating assurance: take refuge in him alone, and he will free Arjuna from all sin, so he need not grieve.
devanagari:
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज ।
अहं त्वां सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥
iast:
sarvadharmānparityajya māmekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja |
ahaṃ tvāṃ sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ ||
english: Let go of all dharmas and take refuge in me alone. I will free you from all sins; do not grieve.

school_notes.note: 'All dharmas' includes adharma, since freedom from all action is meant, citing the Kaṭha Upaniṣad and the Mahābhārata line 'give up both dharma and adharma'.

Keep practising karma, knowledge and bhakti yoga as loving worship, but give them up in the sense of relinquishing fruit, possessiveness and doership, taking me alone as doer, object of worship, goal and means.
Giving up dharma means giving up its fruit; otherwise how could Krishna command Arjuna to fight? As 18.11 says, one who gives up the fruit of action is the true relinquisher.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna tells Arjuna who should not be taught this teaching.
devanagari:
इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन ।
न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति ॥
iast:
idaṃ te nātapaskāya nābhaktāya kadācana |
na cāśuśrūṣave vācyaṃ na ca māṃ yo'bhyasūyati ||
english: This is never to be told by you to one without austerity, or without devotion, or to one unwilling to listen, or to one who finds fault with me.

school_notes.note: This teaching, given for your good to end worldly existence, should not be told to one without austerity, nor to an ascetic lacking devotion to teacher and God, nor to a devotee unwilling to listen.
Do not tell it to one who has not practised austerity, nor ever to one not devoted to you as teacher and to me, nor to a devotee unwilling to listen, nor to one who resents me.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna praises those who pass this teaching on to his devotees.
devanagari:
य इमं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति ।
भक्तिं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः ॥
iast:
ya imaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ madbhakteṣvabhidhāsyati |
bhaktiṃ mayi parāṃ kṛtvā māmevaiṣyatyasaṃśayaḥ ||
english: One who teaches this supreme secret to my devotees, having shown the highest devotion to me, will without doubt come to me.

school_notes.note: Whoever passes on this text, the dialogue of Keśava and Arjuna, to those devoted to me, establishing both its words and meaning as I have for you, will come to me.
Whoever explains this supreme secret among my devotees, with supreme devotion to me, comes to me; there is no doubt of it.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says no one is dearer to him than one who shares this teaching.
devanagari:
न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्चिन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः ।
भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि ॥
iast:
na ca tasmānmanuṣyeṣu kaścinme priyakṛttamaḥ |
bhavitā na ca me tasmādanyaḥ priyataro bhuvi ||
english: No one among people does more to please me than they do, and no one on earth will ever be dearer to me than they are.

school_notes.note: Among people now living, none does greater service to me than one who hands down this teaching, and none in the future will be dearer.
None before and none after; the unfit are mentioned first (18.67) because teaching them is even worse than failing to teach the fit.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says studying this dialogue is itself a form of worship.
devanagari:
अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः ।
ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः ॥
iast:
adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃvādamāvayoḥ |
jñānayajñena tenāhamiṣṭaḥ syāmiti me matiḥ ||
english: And whoever studies this sacred dialogue of ours, by them I would be worshipped through the sacrifice of knowledge: that is my view.

school_notes.note: Among sacrifices, ritual, recited, whispered and mental, the sacrifice of knowledge is best, being mental; studying the Gita is such a sacrifice.
By merely studying this dialogue, I am worshipped with the sacrifice of knowledge described in it.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna says even one who simply listens with faith is freed and reaches the worlds of the righteous.
devanagari:
श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च शृणुयादपि यो नरः ।
सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभाँल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्मणाम् ॥
iast:
śraddhāvānanasūyaśca śṛṇuyādapi yo naraḥ |
so'pi muktaḥ śubhām̐llokānprāpnuyātpuṇyakarmaṇām ||
english: And the person who simply listens, with faith and without finding fault, they too, freed, will reach the auspicious worlds of those who do good deeds.

school_notes.note: 'Even' implies how much more so for one who understands its meaning; freed from sin, the listener reaches the worlds of those who perform rites such as the agnihotra.
Merely by hearing, one is freed from the sins that obstruct devotion and reaches the company of my devotees who do good.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Krishna
context: Krishna asks Arjuna whether he has listened closely and whether his confusion is gone.
devanagari:
कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा ।
कच्चिदज्ञानसंमोहः प्रनष्टस्ते धनंजय ॥
iast:
kaccidetacchrutaṃ pārtha tvayaikāgreṇa cetasā |
kaccidajñānasaṃmohaḥ pranaṣṭaste dhanaṃjaya ||
english: Have you heard this with an attentive mind, son of Pritha? Has your confusion born of ignorance been destroyed, Arjuna?

school_notes.note: Have you grasped what I said with full attention, and is your natural lack of discernment, born of ignorance, gone, which is why this scripture was heard?
Is the ignorance gone that confused you into saying 'I will not fight'?

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Arjuna
context: Arjuna replies that his confusion is gone and his doubts resolved, and that he will act on Krishna's teaching.
devanagari:
नष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत ।
स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥
iast:
naṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtirlabdhā tvatprasādānmayācyuta |
sthito'smi gatasandehaḥ kariṣye vacanaṃ tava ||
english: My delusion is gone, Krishna; by your grace I have regained clear understanding. I stand firm, my doubts gone. I will do as you say.

school_notes.note: Destroyed is the delusion born of ignorance, cause of all worldly evil and hard to cross like the ocean; regained is the remembrance of the self, which loosens all the knots of the heart.
Delusion is wrong knowledge, taking prakṛti for the self; remembrance is knowledge of reality as it is; both changes came by your grace.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sanjaya
context: Sanjaya, concluding his report to Dhritarashtra, says he has heard this wondrous dialogue.
devanagari:
इत्यहं वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः ।
संवादमिममश्रौषमद्भुतं रोमहर्षणम् ॥
iast:
ityahaṃ vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ |
saṃvādamimamaśrauṣamadbhutaṃ romaharṣaṇam ||
english: Thus I have heard this wondrous dialogue between Krishna and the great-souled son of Pritha, which makes my hair stand on end.

school_notes.note: I have heard this dialogue as told, most astonishing and thrilling.
Vāsudeva is the son of Vasudeva, and Pārtha the son of his father's sister, a great soul who has taken refuge at his feet.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sanjaya
context: Sanjaya says that by Vyasa's grace he heard this teaching directly from Krishna.
devanagari:
व्यासप्रसादाच्छ्रुतवानेतद्गुह्यमहं परम् ।
योगं योगेश्वरात्कृष्णात्साक्षात्कथयतः स्वयम् ॥
iast:
vyāsaprasādācchrutavānetadguhyamahaṃ param |
yogaṃ yogeśvarātkṛṣṇātsākṣātkathayataḥ svayam ||
english: By the grace of Vyasa I heard this supreme secret, this yoga, from Krishna, the lord of yoga, himself, as he spoke it directly.

school_notes.note: Through Vyāsa's grace, by gaining divine sight; the text itself is called yoga because yoga is its purpose; heard directly, not passed down.
Through Vyāsa's favour, gaining divine sight and hearing, I heard it directly from Krishna, the treasury of knowledge, strength, lordship, valour, power and splendour.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sanjaya
context: Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra that he rejoices again and again recalling the dialogue.
devanagari:
राजन्संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य संवादमिममद्भुतम् ।
केशवार्जुनयोः पुण्यं हृष्यामि च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
iast:
rājansaṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya saṃvādamimamadbhutam |
keśavārjunayoḥ puṇyaṃ hṛṣyāmi ca muhurmuhuḥ ||
english: O king, as I recall again and again this wondrous and holy dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.

school_notes.note: The dialogue is holy because even hearing it removes sin; recalling it, I rejoice at every moment.
Recalling this holy, wondrous dialogue that I heard directly, I rejoice again and again.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sanjaya
context: Sanjaya says he is filled with wonder recalling Krishna's cosmic form.
devanagari:
तच्च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपमत्यद्भुतं हरेः ।
विस्मयो मे महान् राजन्हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः ॥
iast:
tacca saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya rūpamatyadbhutaṃ hareḥ |
vismayo me mahān rājanhṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
english: And as I recall again and again that most wondrous form of Krishna, great is my amazement, O king, and I rejoice again and again.

school_notes.note: The form meant is the universal form.
The divine form revealed to Arjuna, which I too saw directly; recalling it, my amazement grows and I rejoice again and again.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sanjaya
context: Sanjaya's closing words: where Krishna and Arjuna are, there fortune and victory will be.
devanagari:
यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः ।
तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥
iast:
yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ |
tatra śrīrvijayo bhūtirdhruvā nītirmatirmama ||
english: Wherever there is Krishna, the lord of yoga, and wherever there is the son of Pritha, the archer, there are fortune, victory, prosperity and lasting good policy: that is my conviction.
